mia: Quick sync — I'm putting up a small PR to add a compact 'quant profile matrix' page and two minimal SDK examples (Python + Go) that show batching + kv_prefetch. Also found a couple of 404s under /optimize/quant-profiles. PTAL if you have a minute. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5423
ashwin: Thanks — can you paste the snippets here so I can sanity-check param names?
mia: Sure. Python snippet (tiny):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.generate(
    model="rwd/opt-13b-q4",
    input="Summarize the following...",
    batch_size=8,
    kv_prefetch=True,  # enables prefix/KV prefetch
    quant_profile="q4_256"
)
print(resp.text)
```
mia: Go snippet (even smaller):
```go
import "github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go"
client := sdkgo.NewClient(nil)
resp, _ := client.Generate(ctx, sdkgo.GenerateParams{
    Model: "rwd/opt-13b-q4",
    Input: "Summarize the following...",
    BatchSize: 8,
    KVPrefetch: true,
    QuantProfile: "q4_256",
})
fmt.Println(resp.Text)
```
mia: The key point: use `kv_prefetch` / `KVPrefetch` (not the old `kv_cache` flag) and show a tiny batch_size example so folks see the tradeoff.
sam: @mia — nice. Can you add a short table to the matrix showing expected latency delta and cost delta for q4_256 vs q8_512 at batch sizes 1,4,8? Even a rough ballpark helps readers.
mia: Yep — I'll add a 3-row matrix with latency/cost columns and a note that numbers are workload-dependent. Keeping it conservative.
leila: Also include a one-line Dedicated/Private note: "If you're on Dedicated or Private, pin the quant_profile per model version to avoid rollout surprises."
mia: Good call, adding that in migration notes.
nashwin: About the broken links — which paths?
